sentences.text: The species Ledumahadi mafube is known from a single, incomplete postcranial skeleton of a quadrupedal dinosaur.
It possessed very large and robust forelimbs similar to its relatives, yet its limbs were naturally flexed rather than purely columnar.
Phylogenetic analysis places this animal in the clade Lessemsauridae within the Sauropodomorpha, classifying it as a member of the parent group Sauropodiformes and the dinosaur class Saurischia.
Despite lacking the columnar limbs seen in later giants, Ledumahadi weighed approximately 12 tonnes and is considered the largest land animal to have ever lived during the Early Jurassic epoch.
This massive creature reached a maximum body mass of around 12 tonnes at the age of 14 years.
The genus Ledumahadi was described by McPhee and colleagues in 2018.
Fossils were found in the Early Jurassic Elliot Formation in the Free State Province of South Africa.
Ledumahadi lived between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago during the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages.
It is debated whether the Triassic-Jurassic extinction event had a significant effect on body size evolution in sauropodomorphs, given that Ledumahadi achieved large size shortly after the event.
